atoms.b: Mountains are areas of land that are much ((++higher lower)) than the land surrounding them. In general, they are over ((++600_m 50_km)) high.
Almost 25% of the Earth’s land surface is covered by ((++mountains concrete)). A group of connected mountains is known as a ((++mountain_range volcano)).

feedback.finish: Well known mountain ranges include the Himalayas in Asia and the Andes in South America.

instruction.text: The Alps are the highest mountain range in Europe. Find them on the map.

trainers.hint: This is an elevation map, which shows the changes in the height of land. The lowest areas are shown in green, and the highest are dark red.

feedback.finish: The Alps are a range of mountains spread across multiple countries in Western and Central Europe. The tallest mountain is Mont Blanc, which is a staggering 4,805 metres high!

atoms.a: What do you notice about the location of these mountain ranges?
b: They are all close to each other.
++They lie either on or near tectonic plate boundaries.
They are all below the Equator.

atoms.b: While many mountains lie between two ((++tectonic_plates planets)), some may still be found in the middle of a tectonic plate.
This can be caused by tectonic collisions on boundaries that have long since shifted, or by molten rock pushing up the Earth’s ((++crust grass)).
Examples include the ((++Scottish London)) Highlands and the Appalachian Mountains in the US.
